name: Qwen3.8-27B-opencode-adapted
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear attention with full gated attention every 4th layer (16 of 64); partial RoPE
notes: ADDED 2026-11-22 by the trending sweep. An RL (async-GRPO LoRA) adapter for Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, not a new base model: identical config.json, 27.781B parameters, architecture and KV profile inherited from the base record. It is a PEFT LoRA (library_name peft) - the weights must be merged before serving, and the card also ships a GGUF of the merged model. WHY IT IS A RECORD: it is the first card in this catalog to publish a paired, same-harness base-vs-adapter run on the SWE-bench Pro hard-51 slice with a sign test, and it wins on every axis that matters here: 35.3 -> 51.0 (+15.7) on SWE-bench Pro hard 51, 46.4 -> 52.4 (+6.0) on all 84 graded Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks, and 45.5 -> 59.1 (+13.6, p=0.035) on the 66 Terminal-Bench tasks held out of checkpoint selection. It also does it with fewer tokens: the card reports 13 vs 48 turns on SWE-bench Pro and 3.5x / 2.6x fewer generated tokens on the tasks both solve. HONESTY CHECKS, all from the card itself: (1) the SWE-bench Pro delta is p=0.057 on 51 tasks - directionally clear, statistically not there; only the held-out Terminal-Bench slice clears 0.05. (2) The base column is a real bf16 run of the base model under the same OpenCode harness, not a quant, and the card explicitly warns these numbers are NOT comparable to the Qwen3.8-27B card's 61.7 SWE-bench Pro / 73.0 Terminal-Bench rows, which use Terminus or Claude Code, thinking at maximum effort, larger budgets and the full SWE-bench Pro - so compare this record only against its own base column. (3) Thinking off beats thinking on for this adapter (54.9 with thinking on SWE-bench Pro vs 51.0 off, 56.6 vs 53.0 on Terminal-Bench), i.e. the adapter's gain is not a reasoning-budget artefact. (4) Front-page framing '51.0% vs 47.1%' compares adapter-with-thinking-off against base-with-thinking at xhigh, which is a different comparison from the paired rows recorded here; the paired rows are the honest ones. (5) Sample size is small: 51 and 84 tasks, one attempt each, 95% intervals of +/-13.9 and +/-10.7 points. This is the same lab (harness-hub) as qwen3-8-27b-pi-adapted, a sibling adapter for the PI agent: two adapters on one base, both with paired evidence, and their Terminal-Bench numbers should not be pooled because the harnesses differ (PI vs OpenCode). Hardware gate: 27.8B dense inherited, ~55.6 GFLOPs per generated token, 65536 bytes of KV per token over the 16 full-attention layers.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Pro (hard 51)
benchmarks.config: Card 'Full paired results' table, column 'Qwen3.8-27B-opencode-adapted (step 150)' vs column 'Qwen3.8-27B' at 35.3 for the same 51 tasks: +15.7 points, 11 newly solved / 3 lost, 95% interval +/-13.9, exact sign test p=0.057 (not significant at 0.05). One attempt per task, thinking off, OpenCode harness, 100 agent steps and 2h per task, temperature 0.8 / top-p 1.0. The base column is a real bf16 run of the base model under the identical harness, not another quant. The base is graded on the 51 hardest tasks of SWE-bench Pro only, which is why 35.3 differs from the 61.7 printed on the Qwen3.8-27B card (that row is the full SWE-bench Pro under a different harness).

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
benchmarks.config: Same paired table, all 84 tasks both runs graded: adapter 52.4 vs base 46.4 (+6.0, 13 newly solved / 8 lost, +/-10.7, p=0.38). The card's headline 4-column table prints 53.0 for this adapter because it compares on the 83 tasks all four runs graded - recorded here is the paired 84-task number. Thinking off; thinking adds 56.6 and is described by the card as not significantly better than the 55.4 base-with-thinking row.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1 (66 tasks held out of checkpoint selection)
benchmarks.config: Same card, held-out slice: 45.5 base -> 59.1 adapter, +13.6 +/-11.1, 12 newly solved / 3 lost, p=0.035. Step 150 was selected on SWE-bench Pro plus an 18-task Terminal-Bench 2.1 subset, so this row is the one not contaminated by checkpoint selection. No harness change: OpenCode, one attempt, 100 steps, 1h per task, thinking off.
